steelman: For a practitioner debugging a noisy RAG pipeline, the reflexive fix is a stronger relevance reranker. The thesis says that reflex is misdirected: relevance is the wrong optimization target because it is not the quantity the generator consumes. Two independent 2026 studies converge on this. BAR-RAG shows relevance-only rerankers systematically pick answer-revealing-but-trivial or superficially-relevant-but-incomplete passages, and gets a 10.3% average end-to-end gain by targeting the generator's Goldilocks Zone instead. An Information Gain Pruning study shows retrieval relevance (NDCG) correlates weakly and sometimes NEGATIVELY with end-to-end QA quality (F1), and gets +12-20% relative F1 while cutting final-stage input tokens 76-79%. The precise claim: optimize and rank for marginal generator utility under a token budget, not relevance, and the winning configuration will use FEWER passages than a relevance-maximizing one.
strongest_attack: Trivially-true / says-nothing-non-obvious: 'relevance is not the same as usefulness' is a decades-old IR commonplace (precision-vs-recall, the difference between topical relevance and answer support). Dressing it in two 2026 papers and percentage gains does not make it a new claim; any competent RAG engineer already knows more-relevant is not more-answerable, so the thesis restates folk knowledge as if it were contestable.
reconciliation: The attack does not win. The thesis is sharper than 'relevance != usefulness' in two falsifiable, non-obvious ways. First, the directional claim: not merely that relevance is an imperfect proxy, but that pushing HARDER on relevance (a stronger reranker) fails to fix noise and the correlation with F1 can go NEGATIVE. Folk knowledge says relevance is necessary-but-insufficient; the thesis says at the margin it can be actively anti-correlated with answerability, which contradicts the common expectation that a better reranker monotonically helps. Second, the prescription is concrete and testable: score marginal information gain under a token budget and expect the optimal passage count to DROP (76-79% token cut, fewer passages winning). That is a specific, refutable engineering recipe, not a truism. A single ablation (add a SOTA reranker, measure end-to-end F1) can falsify it; folk truisms cannot be falsified by an experiment.
strengthened_argument: If your RAG answers are noisy, adding a stronger relevance reranker is the wrong lever: across two independent 2026 studies, retrieval relevance (NDCG) correlates weakly and sometimes negatively with end-to-end answer quality (F1), because relevance rankers select answer-revealing-but-trivial or relevant-but-incomplete passages the generator cannot use. Both replace relevance with a generator-utility objective (BAR-RAG's Goldilocks Zone: +10.3% end-to-end; Information Gain Pruning: +12-20% relative F1) and both win with FEWER, denser passages, cutting final-stage tokens 76-79%. Actionable prediction: measure and rerank for marginal generator utility under an explicit token budget, not relevance, and the optimal context will contain fewer passages than a relevance-maximizing configuration. Falsifier: an ablation where a stronger relevance-only reranker monotonically improves end-to-end F1 would sink it.
reason: The thesis is true on current evidence (two independent 2026 sources with quantified end-to-end gains and a stated negative NDCG-F1 correlation), falsifiable (a relevance-reranker-vs-utility ablation directly tests it, and the 'fewer passages win' prediction is refutable), and non-trivial (it makes a directional, prescriptive claim that contradicts the standard reflex to reach for a stronger reranker, going beyond the folk 'relevance != usefulness' point). The strongest attack, that it is a trivially-true restatement, does not win because the sharp version predicts negative correlation and a specific budget-constrained fewer-passage recipe that an experiment could disprove.
